correctness.rationale: For every pair of integer part sizes \(m,n\ge2\) and each real \(t\in[1,2]\), the finite-dimensional dual Lipschitz ball is full-dimensional. Tight-edge connectedness is proved from midpoint saturation and finite slacks. In the strict interior regime \(1<t<2\), the two one-part-saturated families contribute \((2^m-2)2^n\) and \((2^n-2)2^m\), while the no-internal-tight-edge class contributes two, giving \(2(2^m-1)(2^n-1)\). At the equilateral endpoint \(t=1\), nonconstant two-level functions give \(2^{m+n}-2\). At the graph endpoint \(t=2\), cross-edge potential constraints give \(2^m+2^n-2\). All boundary conditions and normalization at the base point are handled. Six exact rational finite checks agree; the theorem for all dimensions rests on the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The facet number of a natural finite-dimensional Lipschitz-free unit ball is determined exactly for every two positive part sizes and a continuum of snowflake exponents. The new interior classification exposes genuine jumps at both limiting metrics and separates the strictly snowflaked complete bipartite geometry from its equilateral and graph-metric endpoint polytopes. This is a complete motivated combinatorial classification, not merely a small instance or reparameterization of a known endpoint.
